name: Eloko
body:
ELOKO
CR 1

XP 200
NE Small fey
Init +6; Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +7

DEFENSE

AC 14, touch 13, flat-footed 12 (+2 Dex, +1 natural, +1 size)
hp 10 (3d6)
Fort +1, Ref +5, Will +4

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., climb 20 ft.
Melee shortspear +3 (1d4+3), 1 bite +3 (1d4+1)
Ranged shortspear +4 (1d4+1)
Special Attacks beguiling chatter, jungle ambush
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 1st, concentration +2)

3/day—charm person (DC 13)

STATISTICS

Str 13, Dex 15, Con 10, Int 11, Wis 12, Cha 13
Base Atk +1; CMB +1; CMD 13
Feats Improved Initiative
Skills Climb +12, Craft (traps) +6, Knowledge (nature) +6, Perception +7, Stealth +12, Survival +4
Languages Common, Sylvan
SQ persuasion, quick hide

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Beguiling Chatter (Su)

An eloko can speak in a beguiling voice causing living creatures within 30 feet (other than eloko and biloko) to become fascinated (DC 12 Will negates) for 2d4 rounds. Fascinated creatures are treated as if two steps more friendly in attitude toward the eloko and will follow a brief, simple, and reasonable request the eloko makes. Creatures that save are immune to that eloko’s beguiling chatter for 24 hours. This is an auditory mind-affecting effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Jungle Ambush (Ex)

An eloko gains a +1 competence bonus on attack rolls against creatures during a surprise round or that are in difficult terrain; these bonuses stack.

Persuasion (Su)

As a biloko.

Quick Hide (Ex)

An eloko in jungle terrain can move 5 feet and make a Stealth check to hide as a swift action, even if it is directly observed.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm forests
Organization solitary, pair, or gang (3-16)
Treasure standard (4 shortspears, other gear)

Biloko (singular and plural) are small, twisted humanoids with gnarled features and sharp claws. These cunning fey inhabit dense jungles, luring travelers with their beguiling words and voracious hunger. They wear clothing made of grass, and some of their kind called eloko may even grow hair and beards of grass and leaves and are usually stronger and even more cunning than typical biloko. Sometimes they carry a small bell whose strange chimes accompany their whispering voices to induce travelers to leave their safe paths and lose themselves in the jungles.

Despite their diminutive size, biloko are fierce predators, wielding crude weapons and traps and preying on the unwary, devouring humanoids with relish. Despite their diminutive size of around 3 to 3-1/2 feet tall, eloko are much stronger than a typical human.
